subject: Renewal discussion: staggered incentive + temporary burst capacity
messages:
From: Sara Morales <sara@nimretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Chavez <paul.procure@nimretail.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning: looking for price stability + short-term burst

Hi Karthik —

Quick note as we start our renewal planning for Nimbus: thanks for the partnership this past year. Our usage doubled during the Q1 promotion window (attached summary) and we expect two additional holiday pushes in H2.

We want to lock a price hold for the coming 12-months, but also need a flexible burst buffer for seasonal spikes (30–40% above committed throughput for up to 10 days per quarter). Can Redwood offer a staggered incentive/credit structure that: (1) preserves a unit price for committed volume, (2) gives predictable, discounted burst buckets we can draw from, and (3) includes a small renewal credit tied to expansion?

High level ask: a one-year renewal, modest uplift in commit (~20%), temporary burst pool, and a $50k renewal credit if we commit to product integration milestones.

Attached: Nimbus_usage_Q1.csv (export).

Would appreciate a short proposal by next week so we can budget accordingly. Looping Paul for procurement timeline.

—Sara
Sara Morales
Head of ML Ops, Nimbus Retail
[sara@nimretail.com]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Morales <sara@nimretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: looking for price stability + short-term burst

Thanks Sara — this is helpful context. I reviewed the usage CSV and talked with product about predictable burst lanes. Monica (CS lead) and Laura (pricing) are cc'd — want to involve them for the detailed economics.

Preliminary approach we can tailor:
- 12-month renewal with a 20% baseline commit uplift (you proposed).
- Burst buckets sold as pre-purchased burst credits: three sizes (5%, 20%, 40%) with tiered discounts; unused burst credits roll forward as part of an annual reconciliation.
- $50k renewal credit tied to two integration milestones (API integration + console audit) — we can phrase as milestone-based credits.

We can produce a short term-sheet that shows per-token effective price under committed volume, burst draw rates, and a runway for true-up. Monica/Laura — can you validate whether a 40% burst for 10 days per quarter is feasible under our capacity model and what discount bands make sense?

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Sara Morales <sara@nimretail.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: looking for price stability + short-term burst

Karthik / Sara — digging into capacity:
- 40% sustained burst for 10 days qtrly is operationally heavy but doable as a pre-purchased tier (we'd need a soft cap to prevent runaway backfill costs). Suggest capped burst credits: e.g., 40% cap but limited to X total token-days per quarter (we will compute X based on the Q1 export).
- Discount bands: 5% burst = no discount (base), 20% burst = 8% discount on burst units, 40% burst = 12% discount. (These are starting points.)
- Renewal credit: prefer to structure $50k as two $25k credits after milestone sign-off to keep legal happy.

I'll assemble a short proposal PDF with the economics and a sample true-up worksheet. Will drop a draft by Friday EOD.

M
Monica Patel
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed-staggered-incentive-v2.pdf (PDF, 68KB)]
From: Sara Morales <sara@nimretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Chavez <paul.procure@nimretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: looking for price stability + short-term burst

Monica — thanks for the detail. The capped burst credit idea sounds reasonable; Paul's procurement team will want clear definitions for the caps and reconciliation timing. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Can burst credits be drawn on-demand (self-serve) and auto-bill against the pre-purchased pool?
- For the integration milestones: the API integration will be done by our platform team; the console audit is internal but we can provide sign-off docs. Splitting the credit is fine, but prefer the first credit to be applied at contract effective date to help cash flow.

Proposed next step: send a redlineable term-sheet + an estimate of how many burst credit units we should pre-buy for a 40% worst-case scenario. If you can include a sample true-up worksheet, we can push this through procurement the week after next.

Thanks — Sara
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Morales <sara@nimretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Paul Chavez <paul.procure@nimretail.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final term-sheet and next steps (attached)

Hi all — attached is the term-sheet (proposed-staggered-incentive-v2.pdf) and a short true-up worksheet. Summary of the negotiated items:

- 12-month renewal (contract effective 2027-07-01).
- Commit uplift: 20% baseline increase; committed units priced at $0.0065/token equivalent.
- Burst credits: three pre-purchased buckets (5%, 20%, 40%) with discounts of 0%, 8%, 12% respectively. 40% bucket capped at 1,200,000 token-days per quarter; unused burst credits roll to year-end true-up.
- Renewal credit: $50,000 total, split as two credits ($25k at contract execution, $25k after milestone 2 sign-off). Sara requested first $25k at effective date — Monica/Laura confirmed internal ok.
- Billing: monthly invoicing with quarterly true-up. Burst draw is self-serve via Console and will decrement the pre-purchased pool; any overage beyond pre-purchased burst will be billed at a premium rate (list in sheet).
- Next steps: Paul/Procurement to review redlineable PDF and return comments; if acceptable, legal will issue DocuSign.

Paul — looping you for procurement timing. Happy to hop on a 30m call early next week to walk through the table.

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
